subject: OKR Handoff & Dependency Playbook — variance + mitigation
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: OKR Handoff & Dependency Playbook — variance + mitigation

Folks — attaching a concise heatmap + raw dependency tracker. Quick summary up front:

- Objective: Improve inference throughput per-dollar by 18% (Q2 target).
- Current status: ~+6% (we're short ~12pp from target).
- Primary variance drivers: longer tail of 2 customer workloads (Acme AI + internal test suites), and a higher-than-expected fraction of 1:1 low-latency calls that don't batch.

Key asks (for QBR prep / leadership huddle):
1) Re-scope: propose we split the objective into two measurable sub-paths — batch-optimizations (low-hanging wins) and latency-SLO work. I have a proposed split in playbook_v1.md (attached).
2) Dependencies: need immediate triage on two items in dependency_tracker.csv:
   - D-73: Acme AI model variant alignment (blocked on version pin from Product).
   - D-89: Edge routing rule that prevents cross-tenant batching (ops config).
3) Headcount/tactics ask: short-term temporary reallocation (2 engineers x 3 weeks) from infra-scaling to batching optimizations; and one senior infra engineer to drive routing change.

QBR deliverable I want to own: a 1-page mitigation plan with committed owners for each dependency and a revised 90-day forecast. Can Laura or Vivek confirm owners by tomorrow?

Attachments: Q2_OKR_heatmap.xlsx (summary + per-initiative impact), dependency_tracker.csv (live tracker), playbook_v1.md (proposed re-scope & playbook).

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior PM, Platform
Redwood Inference

----
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OKR Handoff & Dependency Playbook — variance + mitigation

Priyom — thanks for the clear summary and attachments. Quick responses inline: 

- I can own the owner confirmation for D-73 (Acme AI). I'll reach out to Sasha today and get the version pin (or a clear timeline).
- For D-89 (edge routing), I need Ops to weigh in — Vivek, can you loop in the network team and indicate whether the routing change is low-risk? If it's a kernel-level change we may need a limited maintenance window.

On the re-scope: I like the two-path split. Suggest the playbook include success metrics for each path (e.g., batch: tokens/sec per GPU + expected cost delta; latency-SLO: 95th percentile target). If we can get a prioritized task list for the 2x engineers, I can sign off on short-term reassignments.

I'll sync with HR about temporary reallocation and confirm there's runway for 3 weeks.

-Laura
Director, Product Ops

----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OKR Handoff & Dependency Playbook — variance + mitigation

Agree with the proposed split. Notes from Ops perspective: 

- D-89 (edge routing): preliminary check says change is feasible but requires an update to the routing policy and a canary in US-west first. Risk: potential 0.5% request-failure blip during rollout. Ops can own the change if we schedule a short maintenance window and have automatic fallback. I will assign Vikas (network lead) to put a mitigation runbook together by EOD tomorrow.
- Regarding batching for 1:1 low-latency calls: two tactical approaches — a micro-batching shim at the SDK layer (quickest, <2 weeks) or a deeper runtime coalescing change (higher ROI, 4–6 weeks). I recommend the SDK shim first to capture immediate wins; longer term runtime work can be a separate project.

I'll also flag the headcount ask to Eng managers. If we reassign two engineers, Ops will need a prioritized ticket list to accept the handoff.

-Vivek
VP, Infrastructure

----
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OKR Handoff & Dependency Playbook — variance + mitigation

Thanks — adding two quick practical items I created in Jira to track the work: 
- INF-4821: SDK micro-batching prototype + bench (owner: Maya Srinivasan)
- OPER-1290: Edge routing canary + fallback runbook (owner: Vikas Rao)

I've also attached a short timeline in the Drive folder with checkpoints for the QBR. Priyom — can you confirm whether Acme AI is comfortable with a pinned older variant during the trial? If not, we'll need to include their engineering contact in the runbook.

Jonas
Head of Performance Engineering

----
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Sasha Turner <sasha.turner@acme.ai>, contracts@thirdwave.co
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OKR Handoff & Dependency Playbook — variance + mitigation

Appreciate the quick responses and the Jira entries — that aligns with what I was hoping for. Action summary: 
1) Laura: confirm owner + timeline for D-73 by EOD today (Acme pin) — status: IN PROGRESS.
2) Vivek: Ops will own D-89 runbook + canary plan (OPER-1290) — deliverable: runbook by EOD tomorrow.
3) Jonas: INF-4821 is the micro-batching spike; please kick off and have initial bench results by July 28.
4) Priyom (me): produce one-page mitigation plan + updated forecast by July 20; I'll fold in updates and circulate draft.

If anyone expects blockers to these commitments, flag now so we can escalate before the leadership check-in.

Attachments referenced inline: Q2_OKR_heatmap.xlsx, dependency_tracker.csv, playbook_v1.md

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior PM, Platform
Redwood Inference
